clue.text: Spreads river across five docks

indicators.note: the river is laid across the numeral, spanning it on either side

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
V is the Roman numeral for five
to dock a tail is to cut it short, so docks means lops

explanation.surface: A river flows past five docks, as if describing a harbour scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts DEE either side of V to make DEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that spreads or unfolds gradually is said to grow and evolve, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Olive largely gets stitched up in fiddle

indicators.note: stitching up rearranges the pieces into a new form
most of the name is used, its last letter left off

explanation.surface: Olive gets stitched up in a fiddle, framed by a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the last letter of Olive; 'stitched up' rearranges what is left into VIOL, the old stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle is the informal name for the bowed string instrument.

clue.text: Amounts of water possibly needed in sunlit resort

indicators.note: the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers in a sunny resort may need plenty of water.
explanation.definitionFit: These metric units measure volumes of liquid, water being one example.

clue.text: Light fabric items designed to go over jumpers

definitions.text: Light fabric items designed to go over jumpers

parts.words: Light fabric items designed to go over jumpers
parts.note: jumpers here are skydivers, not sweaters, and the light canopies open over their heads

explanation.surface: Light garments made to be worn over woollen sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is British for a sweater; here it means someone leaping from a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopies of light fabric open above people jumping from aircraft to slow their fall.

clue.text: Slates laid backwards give way

indicators.note: the word for slates is set down in reverse order

parts.note: to slate a play is to criticise it harshly, so slates means pans

explanation.surface: Roof slates set the wrong way round make the roof give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slates' looks like roofing; here it is the verb meaning criticises.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or a branch that suddenly breaks under strain is said to give way.

clue.text: Writer with showy jewellery having little taste

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
bling is flashy, ostentatious jewellery

explanation.surface: A writer wearing showy jewellery shows little taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little taste' looks like a jibe at the bling; it means taking small bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking small bites of food is having a little taste of it.

clue.text: Came first and quietly withdrew

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly
receded means drew back or withdrew

explanation.surface: Someone came first and then modestly withdrew from the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: To go before something in time or order is to come first.

clue.text: Praise where bird nests, going to Spain for liberty

indicators.note: Spain's letter joins on at the end
the bird settles inside the praise as in a nest

parts.note: to laud is to praise
a tit is a small songbird
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Praise for where a bird nests, heading to Spain for its freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is freedom of action or choice, as in being allowed some leeway.

clue.text: Lists gobbling duck and other fowls

indicators.note: the lists swallow the duck, holding it inside

parts.note: rosters are lists of duties or names
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Lists record a duck gobbling food alongside other birds in a farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockerels are male farmyard birds, so they are fowls other than the duck already mentioned.

clue.text: In speech, Shakespearean character facing north wind

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning to face north means reading upwards
the king's name is said out loud, giving a word for an ogling look

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of a Shakespeare tragedy

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean character speaks while facing into a north wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In speech' turns LEAR into LEER; 'facing north' reverses it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel in a fishing line is to wind it onto the spool.

clue.text: Missing parts of muscular body found by hospital dept

parts.note: abs are the abdominal muscles, prominent on a muscular body
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Parts of a muscular body go missing and turn up in a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone missing from a meeting is not present, which is the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Having dropped a name, niece is disposed to be celebrity

indicators.note: the letters are arranged afresh, as things are disposed in a new order
the word name loses the letter given by a, then joins the rest

explanation.surface: A name-dropper's niece is inclined to fancy herself a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having dropped' takes A out of NAME, leaving NME; 'is disposed' rearranges NME with NIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is fame or high standing, the condition of being a celebrity, a near synonym.

clue.text: American music accompanying tango is most crude

parts.note: the blues is a musical form from the American South
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: American blues played alongside a tango makes for the crudest dance music.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are smutty or risqué, so the superlative means the most vulgar.

clue.text: Hopelessly aspiring to be seen around court, working as a lawyer?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the court's abbreviation
the letters are jumbled in a hopeless muddle

explanation.surface: A hopeless aspirant hangs around court, hoping to work as a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopelessly' gives PRAISING, which 'around' wraps about the court abbreviation; the question mark marks lawyering as just one profession said to practise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers and doctors are said to practise their profession, so one working in law is doing so.

clue.text: Stake European thrust into sentry and swore

indicators.note: the stake and European are pushed inside the sentry

parts.note: a sentry is a guard on watch
an ante is a poker stake put in before the deal

explanation.surface: Someone drives a stake into a European sentry and curses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' looks like the definition; it is ANTE, and the definition is 'swore' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear to something is to vouch for it or give a firm promise, as one vouches for a product.

clue.text: Energy put into shaping of ceramic dish

indicators.note: the energy symbol is placed inside the reshaped letters
the clay word is reshaped, giving a new order of letters

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Energy goes into shaping a ceramic dish on the potter's wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaping of' rearranges CERAMIC into ICCRAM, and 'put into' places E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert served in a bowl counts as a dish, in the sense of a course of food.

clue.text: Gross to come in unshaven or moustached

indicators.note: the answer is found coming inside the following words

explanation.surface: Unshaven or moustached men coming in are thought gross.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean very large or bulky, a synonym of huge.

clue.text: Busy, as ladies often seem to be …

definitions.meaning: busy means engaged or in use

definitions.text: as ladies often seem to be
definitions.meaning: the ladies is a women's lavatory, often found engaged with a queue outside

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the ladies' is the women's public toilet, whose lock often reads engaged; ellipses run this clue into the next ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Something occupied is taken or in use, as a busy phone line or a locked toilet cubicle is.

clue.text: The still, small voice opposed to logical observation?

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
science works by systematic, reasoned observation

explanation.surface: An inner voice that quietly resists cold, logical reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: The still small voice is a biblical phrase used for one's inner moral sense of right and wrong.

clue.text: … acute in writing, maybe. Alternatively, there's one's expression when talking …

the way one's speech sounds reveals where one comes from

explanation.walkthrough: 'acute' looks like an adjective for the sharp ladies; it is the stress mark, and 'maybe' flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic such as the acute is a written mark, and a regional pronunciation is a way of speaking.

clue.text: … blank, as gents often are!

definitions.meaning: the gents is a men's lavatory, often found free with no queue

explanation.walkthrough: The gents is the British men's public toilet, whose lock often reads free, in contrast to the ladies at 17.
explanation.definitionFit: Something empty or unoccupied is blank, like a blank stare or an empty cubicle.

clue.text: Visit source of Scottish river

indicators.note: the source of something is its beginning, here the first letter

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone visits the source of a river in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source' looks geographical; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend time as a guest somewhere is a stay or visit, a direct synonym.

clue.text: All-round entertainment mostly about America

indicators.note: only most of the word for about is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: circa means about, used before approximate dates
US is short for United States

explanation.surface: An all-round entertainment show that is mostly about America.
explanation.definitionFit: A big top show is performed in a ring, so it is entertainment staged all round the audience.

clue.text: Flier that shows cockney barber's art

indicators.note: Cockney speakers famously drop the letter H at the start of words

parts.note: a barber's trade is hair
a craft is a skilled art

explanation.surface: A Londoner's barbering shows real artistry.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are East Londoners whose accent drops initial H, so HAIR becomes AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes and helicopters fly, so any such machine is a flier.

clue.text: Mention collecting or looking back can be stimulating

indicators.note: the combined letters are read from right to left
the word for mention gathers the other word inside it

parts.note: to cite is to mention as an example or source

explanation.surface: Mentioning or looking back over things can be stimulating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' builds CITORE, which 'looking back' turns round; 'Mention' looks like the definition but is the verb to cite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sexually arousing is stimulating in a sensual way, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Novel artily involving the Queen should be well-read

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the queen's abbreviation
novel means new, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: An artily written novel involving the Queen should appeal to the well-read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' gives LITARY, which 'involving' wraps round the royal cipher; 'Novel' looks like a book but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary person knows a great deal about books, so is widely read.

clue.text: Ergo Russian's definitely getting something to drink

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: A Russian concludes that they should definitely have a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water or a soft drink is a beverage, something one drinks.

clue.text: Disturbed and elderly, eating junk after lunchtime?

indicators.note: the elderly word takes the others inside, as food goes in

parts.note: aged means elderly

indicators.note: junk is placed after lunchtime in the letters

parts.note: one o'clock is a typical lunchtime, and one is the Roman numeral I
tat is cheap, worthless stuff

explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime is one o'clock, giving I.
